summary: Forest Service lookout on Spencer Butte, Skamania County, WA: D-6 cupola in the 1920s, then a 20-foot L-4 tower (1935 to 1938 by source), removed or destroyed; footings remain on the summit.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin (1920s); 20-foot timber tower with L-4 cab (1938 per most sources; 1935 per two others)
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say both structures were removed or destroyed; footings and a concrete foundation remain on the summit.

access.note: Forest Service Trail 30 runs from trailheads on FR 93. The sources read name no closure or permit requirement.

visit.trail_note: Hike from a trailhead on FR 93, reached by the paved road from FR 25. Sources give the trail length as about 1.5, 1.6 or 3.2 miles one way. No lookout remains to climb.

events.note: Site developed as a lookout with a D-6 cupola cabin. The register says the 1920s; WillhiteWeb and the Forest Lookouts list say 1920
Forest Service trail page and Oregon Hikers date the lookout to 1935; disputed against 1938
WillhiteWeb photo caption says the tower and L-4 were under construction in 1936
20-foot timber tower with L-4 cab; the register, firelookout.com, WillhiteWeb and Forest Lookouts all give 1938
Register and Forest Lookouts list say both structures were removed; no year given
firelookout.com says both structures were destroyed; no year given
Registered July 18, 2012 as US 1346, WA 246; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.proposed: D-6 cupola cabin (1920s), then a 20-foot timber tower with L-4 cab (1938)
corrections.why: The brief's design field names only the L-4 cab and omits the earlier D-6 cupola cabin that the register and WillhiteWeb both describe.
Footings and a concrete foundation are reported on the summit, so 'gone' understates what is there.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1938 per the register, firelookout.com, WillhiteWeb and the Forest Lookouts list; 1935 per the Forest Service trail page and Oregon Hikers; a WillhiteWeb photo caption places construction in 1936. The story gives the disagreement and does not pick one.

Register says both structures were removed; firelookout.com says destroyed; Forest Lookouts says removed. Footings and a foundation are reported on the summit, so the story says some remains are there.
The register says the 1920s; WillhiteWeb and the Forest Lookouts list say 1920. The story names both.
Oregon Hikers gives about 1.5 miles from either FR 93 trailhead, WillhiteWeb gives 1.6 miles one way, and the Forest Service gives 3.2 miles one way from the south. The story reports all three.

sources.title: Spencer Butte Lookout Site and Breezy Point

notes_for_editor: Brief checked: the 2012 registration and 4,247 ft elevation agree with the register. height_m 6.1 is the 20-foot tower converted; no source gives a metric height. The construction year is disputed three ways (1935, 1936 photo caption, 1938), and the story reports all three. The brief's design field (L-4) is incomplete and is corrected. Status is proposed as ruins because footings and a foundation are reported on the summit. No staffing or fire history appears in the sources read, so none is recorded. Breezy Point (Trail 30A), a separate patrol point with a fire finder base, is not covered here.
